title: Auto Loans: Undiscounted Rate When Autopay Ends
content:
When autopay is cancelled on an Auto Loans account, the new APR is built up from a starting figure: the loan's rate as it would stand with no discount in it. This note defines that starting figure.

## Definition

The undiscounted rate is the APR on the loan's record with the recorded discounts added back:

- the autopay discount is added back when the loan's recorded discount list names autopay;
- the relationship discount is added back when the list names relationship;
- whatever is added back is counted, in total, at no more than the product's combined discount limit.

The discount sizes and the limit are those of the loan's product.

## Truth table

| Recorded discount list | Amount added back to the recorded APR |
|---|---|
| none | nothing |
| autopay only | the autopay discount |
| relationship only | the relationship discount |
| both autopay and relationship | the sum of the two discounts or the combined limit, whichever is smaller |

## Worked example (invented figures, not the product's actual discounts)

Recorded APR 6.80, recorded list naming both discounts, each discount hypothetically 0.30, combined limit hypothetically 0.50. The two sum to 0.60, the limit holds the add-back to 0.50, and the undiscounted rate is 7.30. Had the list named autopay only, the add-back would be 0.30 and the undiscounted rate 7.10.
